notes: The gold set covered only municipal sewage reports, so it could not detect a
regression in the domains the widened extraction prompt just opened. This page
is deliberately as unlike a water report as the corpus allows: a city booster
magazine, set in narrow columns, describing a school system. Nothing on it is
a concentration, and its unit is the counted noun throughout.

annotation_caveat: Judgement calls, recorded so the accuracy figure can be argued with:
INCLUDED as a standard: 'students over 14 years of age' is an eligibility
threshold for the vocational schools, which is what a standard is -- a rule of
its era rather than a measurement of the world.
EXCLUDED, though numeric: grade levels ('French begins in grade seven',
'funding continues only as far as grade 10', 'kindergarten through grade 13').
These are positions in a sequence, not quantities of anything, and counting
them as measurements would make a trend line out of a curriculum.
EXCLUDED: 'many students have to travel more than a mile'. The number is real
but the subject is 'many students', so there is no quantity to attach it to.
